Industry News: Thune will lead Republicans through the minority

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1070 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., leaves a meeting in the Capitol on Tuesday, before his election as incoming minority leader later in the day.
  • Senate Majority Leader John Thune was reelected as the Republican leader on Tuesday and will steer the conference through their time in the minority.
  • The South Dakotan ran uncontested despite a push from some of his colleagues to delay the leadership elections following Republicans’ stunning defeats last week in the midterms, which saw them lose at least seven seats and the majority.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., leaves a meeting in the Capitol on Tuesday, before his election as incoming minority leader later in the day. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

Senate Majority Leader John Thune was reelected as the Republican leader on Tuesday and will steer the conference through their time in the minority.

The South Dakotan ran uncontested despite a push from some of his colleagues to delay the leadership elections following Republicans’ stunning defeats last week in the midterms, which saw them lose at least seven seats and the majority.

Recent findings suggest that “Obviously, the election result was not what we hoped for,” Thune told reporters, referring to the midterms. “But I think it’s important that we take the lessons from that and internalize the message the American people were sending to us.”.

While he and the rest of the leadership slate sailed through the conference contests by voice vote, it wasn’t without drama.

According to recent reports, before the leadership elections began in the Old Supreme Court Chamber early Tuesday morning, the conference held a meeting at the request of a group of GOP five senators, led by Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis.

According to recent reports, the conversation, which several senators described as “frank,” ended up pushing back the leadership elections by a few hours. But they were not postponed to another day as some had hoped.

“This has never been anything against John Thune,” remarked Johnson, as he made good on his commitment to leave the room early if the conference proceeded with its election. “What I didn’t agree with was holding the election right away, giving nobody an opportunity to really challenge any leadership position.”.

“Part of the concern here is who wants the job? God bless him for serving,” Johnson added.

The conference conversation Tuesday morning turned into an “open-mic” with both conservatives and those who lost their elections speaking, according to senators.

Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., told reporters, “To rush into this and to just ratify all the same leadership — I mean, what message does that send?”.

According to recent reports, but no contender to Thune emerged despite the angst, and a motion to proceed to the election, introduced by Thune’s fellow South Dakotan Sen. Mike Rounds, was accepted.

Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., said voters who rejected Republicans last week were reacting to high gas prices, the war in Iran and the cost of living, not to how Senate leaders were running the conference.

“I don’t think anybody in Texas who voted for the Democrat governor was voting against John Thune. If you diagnose that as a problem, you’re misdiagnosing the problem,” Paul said.

It has been revealed that whip John Barrasso, R-Wyo., was reelected to his position, as was the chairman of the Senate Republican Conference, Tom Cotton of Arkansas. Sen. James Lankford of Oklahoma was again selected as vice chair of the conference, while Sen. Shelley Moore Capito of West Virginia was reelected as Republican Policy Committee chair.

In a recent development, “Our first step is to make sure the American people know that we heard what they stated, and the American people’s priorities are our priorities. That’s the way we regain their trust,” Barrasso said afterward.

Industry observers note that sen. Bernie Moreno of Ohio got the nod to chair the National Republican Senatorial Committee, meaning he will helm the campaign arm as the party looks ahead to the uncertain waters of 2028.

It has been revealed that moreno remarked, “I was in the retail automobile business, so when you don’t listen to your customers, your customers punish you. I think we have to own it, and I think we have to learn from it.”.

Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., stated on Monday evening, “What we as a conference right now need is honesty. We need focus. We need to try to reach a consensus on what we need to change.”.

Kennedy was among those pushing to delay the leadership elections and told reporters on Tuesday he voted present instead of yes on whether to proceed to them.

According to recent reports, sen. Rick Scott, R-Fla., who ran for GOP leader twice — once in 2022 against Sen. Mitch McConnell, R-Ky., and in 2024 against Thune — declined to run again to challenge Thune. But in a Dear Colleague letter on Monday, he detailed what he’d like to see in the lame-duck session before Democrats take power, including confirming every nominee President Donald Trump has sent to the Senate, funding the government without an omnibus, banning stock trading, passing the permitting bill that is advancing this week in the Senate, passing the National Defense Authorization Act, balancing the budget and pushing through a sweeping voter ID bill known as the SAVE America Act.

Senate Republicans on Tuesday also voted on a resolution on their path forward that was spurred by a motion from Scott, aides noted.

“It is the sense of the GOP Conference that we will maximize the 54 days we have with congressional majorities, to confirm every judicial nominee and every executive nominee that the conference approves of, to pass our core Republican priorities, and to do everything humanly possible to pass a reconciliation bill before Jan. 3,” the resolution reads in part.

That long list of goals highlights the expectations Thune has faced as leader, where he led one-third of Republicans’ trifecta in Washington. In the next Congress, Democrats will hold the majority in both chambers of Congress after their larger-than-expected wins, while Trump finishes out his term as president.

Thune stated he told his conference: “As I look back on the last couple of years, my question is, what would you have me do differently?”.

“Given the constraints we had to deal with, all the stuff that was coming at us on a daily basis, a narrow margin in the House, the White House, the Democrats over here who were obstructing two long government shutdowns — I think we came out of it as well as could have been expected, and got a lot of stuff done,” Thune told reporters.

Sources indicate that “If you believe the exit polls, it was the war, it was the economy, it was inflation, it was fuel prices,” Thune added. “So no, I wasn’t apologizing for anything that we did. And I think on the political side, I don’t know what else I could have done.”.

How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love Wrapping Gifts

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that I am one of the messiest people I know, and I come by that reputation honestly.
  • Industry observers note that I’ve inherited her struggles with neatness and attention to detail.
  • When it comes to Christmas, my mom and I have always been aligned on caring more about gathering the people we love to drink mulled wine and watch A Diva’s Christmas Carol for the hundredth time than creating some holiday tableau fit for Instagram.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that I am one of the messiest people I know, and I come by that reputation honestly. Legend has it that when my parents first met at a party at my mom’s apartment, my dad walked up to her to say that she should probably call the police; he’d passed her bedroom while in search of the bathroom and seen the window wrenched open, with belongings strewn all over the floor. He suggested that she report a robbery—but no, she was forced to admit; that was just how she lived.

Industry observers note that I’ve inherited her struggles with neatness and attention to detail. While other mother-daughter duos brought in perfectly stenciled posters and Balthazar-quality brownies to class presentations and bake sales, our attempts were somewhat more haphazard, typically following screaming fights in the aisles of the Staples on 81st and Broadway about what qualified as “nice” graph paper.

When it comes to Christmas, my mom and I have always been aligned on caring more about gathering the people we love to drink mulled wine and watch A Diva’s Christmas Carol for the hundredth time than creating some holiday tableau fit for Instagram. Yet this holiday season finds me in a latest place in my life. Since going through a major breakup last year, I’ve tackled all kinds of things that I didn’t previously know I could do, from fixing my hyperactive car battery without a man’s paid-for help to retiling my very own bathroom floor. Was it possible that I could also become the kind of person who looked forward to—or at least didn’t totally dread—my very least favorite Christmas chore, wrapping presents?

I love shopping, I love seeing someone open what I’ve bought for them, and when I was a kid, I loved carrying already-wrapped gifts down the stairs and arranging them under the tree. But there’s something about the finicky, frilly act of wrapping and taping and bow-tying that makes me revert to that chaotic middle-schooler with the slapped-together bake sale contribution; I hate it, but I also hate hating it.

Industry observers note that so, a few weeks ago, I decided to break the cycle. I contacted It’s A Wrap, a gift-wrapping studio and floral boutique in Studio City, Los Angeles, to ask one simple question: Could a Christmas flop like me really be taught to make a gift look great?

Y Lane, who co-owns It’s A Wrap with partner Carolyn Haywood, has seen it all when it comes to outlandishly LA-coded gifting requests. (Ask her about the time she gift-wrapped a flat-screen TV for a guy’s Playboy Bunny girlfriend on Christmas Day.) But her patience as she walked me through the basics of wrapping—assembling a box; figuring out how much tape to use; creating clean, crease-free corners—was still amazing, given that I’ve had not one but two driving instructors quit on me and, for all I know, made any number of math and science tutors seek workers’ compensation.

I’m far from Y Lane’s first student; she offers gift-wrapping lessons semi-regularly at It’s A Wrap’s cozy, Santa’s-workshop-reminiscent storefront off Tujunga Avenue (that is, if Santa’s workshop were regularly passed by shirtless bros and Alo-clad beach babes sipping iced lattes from Aroma down the street). Demand predictably increases during the holiday season, which, for her, starts well before Halloween and stretches until the beginning of January.

I got the parts with the box and the paper pretty quickly, but once we got into the specifics of bow-tying, my mind went blank. I couldn’t tie a bow in my ponytail for school spirit day or French-braid the other girls’ hair at camp to save my life, so why would I be able to now?

According to recent reports, slowly but surely, though, my efforts came together into a sort-of bow, which Y Lane complimented and then promptly untied, instructing me to try a few more. “The nicer the box is, the easier it is to wrap,” Y Lane told me. “The most vital word in wrapping is measure.”.

Sources indicate that A few weeks later, I have a stack of neatly wrapped gifts piled up under my little pink tree impressively early. And who’s to say? Maybe I’ll also become the person who saves the wrapping paper for next year.

  • President Donald Trump's Republican nominee to the Federal Communications Commission faced opposition Tuesday from Senate Democrats who fear the commission could be controlled exclusively by Republicans under Chairman Brendan Carr, who they vowed to investigate in the next Congress.
  • Appearing before the Senate Commerce Committee, nominee Danielle Thumann Severs limited her commitments to independence from Carr, including on regulating broadcasters based on their content decisions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that FCC nominee Danielle Thumann Severs waits to testify during her confirmation hearing with the Senate Commerce Committee on Tuesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

President Donald Trump's Republican nominee to the Federal Communications Commission faced opposition Tuesday from Senate Democrats who fear the commission could be controlled exclusively by Republicans under Chairman Brendan Carr, who they vowed to investigate in the next Congress.

Appearing before the Senate Commerce Committee, nominee Danielle Thumann Severs limited her commitments to independence from Carr, including on regulating broadcasters based on their content decisions.

Much of the hearing focused on Carr and his threats to use the FCC to punish broadcasters he disagrees with.

It has been revealed that sen. Ben Ray Luján, D-N.M., mentioned that he expects Carr will not last long in his position once Democrats take control of Congress in the upcoming year.

“Mr. Carr, if you're listening now, know you're going to be in this body once a month, if not more, and in the House of Representatives as well, answering questions … so we can get to the bottom of the nonsense and the cover-ups that have been taking place,” Luján mentioned.

Industry observers note that the nomination of Thumann Severs, who currently serves as senior counsel to Carr, has led to consternation among Democrats due to continued vacancies at the FCC. The five-member commission is intended to have three members of the president’s party, including the chair, and two in the minority.

According to recent reports, presently Carr serves alongside fellow Republican Olivia Trusty and Democrat Anna M. Gomez, whose term expired earlier this year. Gomez may continue to serve through next year under the law if a replacement is not nominated and confirmed.

Democrats are concerned that if Thumann Severs were to be confirmed, the commission’s three Republican members could constitute a quorum on their own, allowing Trump to fire Gomez.

Industry observers note that sen. John Hickenlooper, D-Colo., remarked Senate precedent is to move pairs of one Democratic and one Republican nominee for the FCC and that he “strongly” believed the Thumann Severs nomination should have been paired with a renomination of Gomez in order to continue having “both parties at the table.”.

“A bipartisan FCC is essential to avoid things like large-scale media consolidation [and] I think also, more fundamentally, to protect a free and diverse press [that] serves everyone,” Hickenlooper mentioned.

In addition to urging Trump to renominate Gomez, Democrats underlined the need for a second Democratic member of the commission.

Hickenlooper highlighted Thumann Severs’ close work with Carr, who Democrats and some Republicans have been critical of for comments about using the FCC’s public interest standard against television stations airing programming Carr disagrees with.

Thumann Severs’ work at the FCC presently focuses on the Wireline, Public Safety and Homeland Security, and Consumer and Governmental Affairs bureaus, rather than the Media Bureau.

Industry observers note that committee Chair Ted Cruz, R-Texas, has also been critical of Carr’s comments. On Tuesday, he listed the FCC’s request for ABC-owned stations to submit early license renewals alongside earlier incidents in which he remarked Democrats encouraged the weaponization of the FCC against conservative voices.

According to recent reports, “The First Amendment places important limits on the government’s ability to regulate speech,” Cruz said. “The FCC possesses significant regulatory authority over communications, so there is always a risk that it could weaponize its authority against Americans with whom it disagrees.”.

Thumann Severs committed to Cruz that she would base licensing decisions on “the law and the record” and not use the FCC’s authority to “pressure or punish” broadcasters for protected speech.

However, when Sen. Edward J. Markey, D-Mass., questioned Thumann Severs on whether the FCC could punish broadcasters the president disagreed with, Thumann Severs repeated one of Carr’s arguments in discussing the FCC’s role.

“Broadcasters are subject to public interest obligations as part of the public trustee model in exchange for the licenses that they hold,” she said. “As part of those public interest obligations, they are subject to many different rules and requirements, and the FCC is charged with enforcing and investigating the public interest standard against broadcasters.”.

Under repeated questions from Markey about Carr’s previous remarks, Thumann Severs said she would base her decisions “in the facts and the law and the record.”.

Sources indicate that luján also asked Thumann Severs to name issues where she had disagreed with Carr or Trump. While she stated her decisions would be her own, she declined to name any examples of disagreement.

In addition to questions about Carr, Democrats asked the nominee about the FCC’s E-Rate program, which provides low-cost connectivity for schools and libraries, and the Universal Service Fund, which funds the E-Rate program and other programs.

Thumann Severs said that she believes the E-Rate program has been successful and that the FCC has a statutory obligation to provide some kind of discounted service to schools and libraries. But she was less forthcoming on whether the FCC could shut down the program as it currently exists without congressional approval or whether the program should be restricted only to rural areas.

Late last month, Democratic members of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, led by Communications and Technology Subcommittee ranking member Doris Matsui, D-Calif., sent a letter to Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., and Cruz urging Gomez’s renomination with any move to confirm a Republican nominee.

“Commissioner Gomez has shown the experience and judgment to continue that work,” the members wrote. “We therefore ask that the Senate pair any latest Republican nominee with her renomination to a full term, consistent with the bipartisan design Congress built into this agency.”.

On Monday, the Leadership Conference on Civil and Human Rights also sent a letter to committee leadership urging a delay on the hearing and any vote on Thumann Severs’ nomination until Gomez can be renominated.

“Independent agencies should not be extensions of presidential will: their leaders should exercise independent judgement based on their expertise and statutory mandates,” the group wrote.

Cruz did not indicate Tuesday when the committee might vote on Thumann Severs’ nomination, and no markup has yet been unveiled by the committee of hers' and those of three others for two posts at NASA and one at the Transportation Department who also testified.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is a Japanese-style rice porridge known as okayu. I ate this every morning in the early weeks of postpartum after my first daughter was born. It’s what our family reaches for whenever we need a simple, nourishing dish that warms from the inside out. For the smoothest porridge, let the rice soak in cold water before cooking.

If you have time, soak the rice, which makes the texture softer and can aid in digestion. Place washed rice in a bowl and pour in water to cover by 1". Soak at least 30 minutes and up to 4 hours. Drain off excess water before starting the recipe. The wakame seaweed, which you’ve probably had in miso soup, can typically be found dried anywhere Asian groceries are available.

According to recent reports, in The Fourth Trimester, we ask parents: What meal nourished you after welcoming your baby? This month it’s a cozy rice porridge by Eating at Home cookbook author Trinity Mouzon Wofford. Read more: Breakfast at Home, After Birth at Home.

In a recent development, combine 1 cup short-grain rice, washed, soaked if desired, ¼ cup dried wakame (seaweed), 1 Tbsp. dried red shiso, and 6 cups low-sodium broth (any kind) or water in a large donabe, medium Dutch oven, or other heavy pot. Cover and bring to a boil over medium-high heat (you’ll hear bubbling). Uncover and stir, making sure nothing is stuck to bottom of pot. Cover and reduce heat to low. Continue to cook porridge 30 minutes more (resist the urge to peek).

Industry observers note that remove pot from heat and let porridge sit (still covered) 10 minutes. Uncover and stir. Rice grains should be cooked through, broken open, and creamy, but porridge should still be fairly loose. Season porridge with fine sea salt.

Ladle porridge into bowls and serve, topped with toasted sesame seeds, toasted sesame oil, and/or thinly sliced scallions.

The Best Eye Makeup to Wear Over 40, From Cream Shadows to Soft Liners

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (859 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor.
  • According to recent reports, let’s be clear: there are no age-specific makeup rules.
  • Sources indicate that before choosing colors, take a look at your current products to assess textures.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

According to recent reports, let’s be clear: there are no age-specific makeup rules. Wear whatever shade or trend you feel best in, no matter your age. That mentioned, it’s no secret that our facial features change as we get older, and to keep looking your best, the skin care and makeup products in your rotation may need to be adjusted accordingly. After 40, that powder eye shadow that once looked perfect across a smooth eyelid may now crease and settle into fine lines. Or your signature eyeliner may have started to look a little less visible because of eyelid hooding. Maybe your lashes are more sparse? Before dumping your entire eye makeup kit, take some cues from a pro on choosing and wearing the best eye makeup after 40.

Sources indicate that before choosing colors, take a look at your current products to assess textures. “As we get older, the skin on our eyelids gets thinner, and a little more crinkled, so heavy or dry powder shadows can settle into fine lines and actually emphasize them,” celebrity makeup artist Brandy Allen tells ELLE. You’ll want to swap out chalky, dry formats for cream-based shadows and liners.

It has been revealed that how you treat the skin in your eye area matters too—both for how well and how long the makeup wears. Allen recommends using an eye cream or eye patches to hydrate the skin. “I have been loving the Parivie Smooth & Brighten Eye Masks because of the collagen and skin-loving ingredients they have,” notes Allen. “Give the leftover serum a minute to sink in, and then go in with a thin layer of primer like the Urban Decay Eyeshadow Primer Potion so your shadow has something to grip onto and stays crease-free all day,” Allen suggests.

Many hybrid products now combine skin care with color cosmetics. A win-win for aging skin. Look for hydrating ingredients like hyaluronic acid, smoothing niacinamide, ceramides, and squalene that will treat skin while delivering solid color payoff.

Saie SuperSuede Baked Eyeshadow.

16-hour wear; infused with jojoba esters, ceramides, hyaluronic acid, squalane.

Laura Mercier Matte Caviar Stick Eye Shadow.

Available in 32 shades; waterproof and sweatproof; formulated with hyaluronic acid and firming raspberry stem cell extract.

RMS Beauty Eyelights Cream Eyeshadow.

Comes in 11 colors; buildable; has antioxidant-rich green tea extract and a smoothing natural peptide quinoa extract.

ILIA The Necessary Eyeshadow Palette.

A mix of matte, satin, and metallic finishes; formulated with moisturizing jojoba seed oil and antioxidant-rich vitamin E.

Look for creamy formulas that blend easily like the M.A.C Dazzleshadow Eye Shadow Stick. These will crease less. “It has a soft metallic shine and 12-hour wear, and it doubles as a liner, so it’s an easy one-step product,” Allen notes.

According to recent reports, satin and soft-sheen finishes are the best here, too. Allen notes they give the lid a little luminosity that reflects light, which makes the eye area look more lifted and fresh. “A finely milled shimmer on the center of the lid is great too, especially for the holidays. If you prefer a powder, I love the Jones Road The Best Eyeshadow. It has a soft texture that blends out so easily, and it comes in both matte and shimmer finishes.”.

It has been revealed that allen indicates soft, warm neutrals like taupes, espresso and chocolate browns, bronze, and soft rose gold tones are most flattering for 40 and over eyes. “I’d also recommend swapping a jet-black liner for a deep brown. Brown still defines the eye but looks softer and less harsh against the skin.” Allen’s top pick is the Glampton Cream Eyeshadow & Gel Liner Duo in Espresso & Rose Gold, which she says is a great option here because it gives you both shades in one. “The shadow stick is creaseless, blends out with just your finger, and the gel liner glides on without tugging on the lid,” Allen notes.

Just because your skin is maturing doesn’t mean you can’t try trends. Allen says it’s more about adjusting the trend to work for you. “The lived-in, smudged smoky eye trend is actually great for more mature skin; just keep it soft, and focus the liner on the outer half of the lower lash line instead of going all the way around,” says Allen. One product she suggests avoiding is chunky glitter, as it can settle into lines and emphasize texture.

Once your products are in place, perfect your application technique. It’ll make a difference. “When blending shadow, angle it upward toward the tail of your brow instead of dragging it down. This gives the eye an instant lift,” Allen instructs. You can also tap a little rose gold or champagne shimmer onto the inner corners and center of the lid to brighten. And don’t forget the under-eyes and brows. “A color corrector like the Bobbi Brown Skin Long-Wearing Color Corrector Stick cancels out darkness, and well-groomed, filled-in brows frame the whole eye area,” Allen explains.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that thanksgiving is practically an Olympic event for eating, but there’s nothing wrong with a little warm-up the night before. Chipotle is bringing back its Thanksgiving Eve BOGO deal, giving you a perfectly good excuse to grab a burrito with an old friend before the turkey, stuffing, and inevitable food coma take over.

The deal runs Wednesday, November 25, from 5 to 9 p.m. local time at participating U.S. restaurants, with the usual buy one entrée, get one free format we all know and love.

But, as expected, there’s some fine print worth reading before you get in line. You’ll need to be a Chipotle Rewards member, order at the restaurant, and scan your Rewards card at checkout. The free entrée must cost the same as or less than the one you're buying, and you can claim up to five free entrées per check. Kids’ meals don't qualify, and ordering ahead through the app, online, or for delivery won't work.

Recent findings suggest that the timing has changed a bit from last year, too, when it ran from 4 p.m. all the way until closing. This time, you've got a four-hour window, so make sure that one friend you have who’s perpetually late gets the memo.

“The response last year showed us how much our guests embraced the occasion,” Stephanie Perdue, Chipotle's senior vice president of brand marketing, mentioned in a statement. According to the chain, the promotion ended up being its biggest sales-driving campaign of 2025, so a return trip was probably inevitable.

In a recent development, and if you’re stuffed and don’t feel like leaving the couch the next day, there’s a little something for the post-Thanksgiving crowd as well. From Friday, November 27, through Monday, November 30, Chipotle is waiving its delivery fee on eligible orders placed through its app or website with code CYBER26. You’ll need to spend at least $10 in the U.S. or $12 in Canada, and delivery menu prices may be higher, with other fees still applying.

If nothing else, it’s a convenient excuse to take a break from the annual challenge of finding increasingly creative ways to eat leftover turkey.

More Democrats emerged Tuesday wanting someone besides Senate Democratic leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., to lead their conference in the majority.

Recent findings suggest that but Schumer maintained confidence he would be reelected to the post despite Sens. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., publicly calling for a different leader or a “concrete plan” that provides change.

“I’m confident I will be elected majority leader, and our caucus is really united in focusing on bringing down costs, on ending the corruption, on ending the chaos, on ending the war,” Schumer told reporters Tuesday. “We have great unity in our caucus, and I’ll be proud to lead it.”.

Sanders remarked during a news conference Tuesday the election was about “change and the need for the Democratic Party to move in a new and bold direction.”.

“I personally have known Chuck Schumer for over 30 years, and I like Chuck. Nobody works harder than Chuck Schumer. But in my view the time is now for change, and I will not be supporting Chuck to be reelected as the Democratic leader,” Sanders stated, calling for an “economy that works for all, not just the people on top.”.

“Do I think Chuck has been leading in that direction?” he asked. “No.”.

Some incoming members and now incumbents have pointed to Maryland Democrat Chris Van Hollen as one possibility to challenge Schumer. Van Hollen had previously thrown cold water on the idea by saying he was instead “kicking the tires” on a presidential run in 2028 but has recently changed his tune.

A person familiar with Van Hollen’s thinking noted he “has received an outpouring of calls on running for majority leader and is now in active listening mode.”.

Slotkin did not endorse anyone for leader but said she had a “really productive conversation” with Van Hollen yesterday.

In a recent development, “Whoever wants my vote is going to have to show me a concrete initiative that’s definitely different. I’m a ‘no’ until and unless I see that from anyone,” she stated, urging her peers to “withhold quorum” when Senate Democrats hold their leadership elections “until you get that plan and you feel like you have a voice in that plan.”.

Recent findings suggest that she urged not just a roadmap for the first 100 days, but ideas for how to “communicate differently.” As for her own future, she said, “I am not actively seeking this job. I’m seeking change.”.

Asked about his plans Monday evening, Van Hollen said, “It’s not about me, but I am listening to the thousands of people who have been calling for change, but especially listening to our members, with a particular ear to upcoming members who have just come off the campaign trail.”.

In a recent development, “What I’ve said from the very beginning is, we shouldn’t have a coronation. We should have a caucus discussion about what we're going to do with the power and responsibilities that have been invested in us,” Van Hollen said. “I’m in listening mode and haven’t shut the door.”.

Van Hollen took it a step further at an event Tuesday in Washington, D.C., criticizing the minority leader and Democrats’ campaign arm over their preferences in some primaries. “Schumer and the DSCC sided with the crypto industry and AIPAC against these candidates,” he said, according to a livestream of the event.

In a recent development, schumer tried to tamp down the suggestion of a rivalry. “We talk frequently, and we’re united — united in lowering costs, and united in ending this damn war,” he remarked of Van Hollen.

Others threw their support behind Schumer ahead of the Democratic leadership elections, which are expected to take place in December.

Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee Chair Kirsten Gillibrand, D-N.Y., praised Schumer for raising money and recruiting candidates like Sens.-elect Sherrod Brown of Ohio and Roy Cooper of North Carolina to help land at minimum seven seats, and potentially nine if Alaska and Mississippi ultimately swing their way.

“That takes vision. It takes clarity of thought. It takes strategic leadership, and that is what Sen. Schumer has done. And that is why you will see, despite all grumblings, enormous gratitude,” she stated.

Gillibrand pointed to candidates like Scott Colom, the Democrat in Mississippi who is at the moment leading GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in a nail-biter of a race. “That wave doesn’t get created by magic. It gets created by hard work and putting the pieces together over years,” she said.

Colom, however, has been noncommittal, telling MS NOW, “Too many of our leaders are from the same areas of the country,” pointing to the Brooklyn roots of both Schumer and current House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, who is expected to run for speaker on the House side.

Sen. Ruben Gallego, D-Ariz., mentioned he and Schumer have had their differences. But he implied he backs him for majority leader: “At the end of the day, these are historic numbers. It’s time for us to unify. We are going to work together as a caucus to plan together about how to move forward for what the country wants us to do, and I think we have the person who I think is going to lead us there.”.

Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., remarked Democrats have “an opportunity to do things differently, and I think we will, regardless of who the leader is. It doesn’t really matter whose name is on the door.”.

“Yes,” he mentioned of his support for Schumer, noting that so far, nobody has officially stepped up to the plate. “This is a guy that worked incredibly hard over the last couple of years. I know people have other opinions about this. But we have a mandate to do things and get things done for the American people.”.

“And we can do that with Chuck Schumer.”.

Apple Juice Bread

📅 22 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (709 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Epicurious

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A simple swap from water to apple juice transforms this basic bread recipe into a subtly sweet loaf that is perfect to tear into at breakfast time with a smear of good butter on top, but it also takes a PB&J to the next level.
  • Sources indicate that I first encountered the idea at the small four-seat teppanyaki restaurant in the back of the Suiran Hotel in Kyoto, Japan, where chef Tsubasa Yamaguchi served it before my first course; it was a perfect way to start the meal.
  • Take care when you’re lowering the bread into the Dutch oven; it is a slightly nerve-wracking moment but a little attention is all that’s needed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A simple swap from water to apple juice transforms this basic bread recipe into a subtly sweet loaf that is perfect to tear into at breakfast time with a smear of good butter on top, but it also takes a PB&J to the next level. The subtle, but unmistakable, undercurrent of apple sweetness struck me as a bit of a magic trick in a bread that, otherwise, to the eye and hand was just a soft white loaf.

Sources indicate that I first encountered the idea at the small four-seat teppanyaki restaurant in the back of the Suiran Hotel in Kyoto, Japan, where chef Tsubasa Yamaguchi served it before my first course; it was a perfect way to start the meal. When I asked him what he did differently to prepare it, he said he just took the same rustic bread recipe he baked elsewhere and used apple juice in place of water. I was incredulous. That was it? The same amount? The same technique? Yes and yes, he said. I was hooked. It turns out the water-to-juice switcheroo gives an added taste of fall without taking anything away from the shape and texture. It’s become an instant favorite at my house both breakfast and lunch, and I expect it will be at yours.

Take care when you’re lowering the bread into the Dutch oven; it is a slightly nerve-wracking moment but a little attention is all that’s needed. You can do it!

More apple recipes here: 37 Apple Desserts That Make Us Want to Pick the Whole Orchard.

Mix 4 cups (500 g) all-purpose flour, 1¾ cups apple juice, 1 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, 1 Tbsp. sugar, and one ¼-oz. envelope instant yeast (about 2¼ tsp.) in a large bowl just until flour is hydrated and a very shaggy dough forms, about 1 minute. Cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit at room temperature 15 minutes.

Set a small bowl of room-temperature water on work surface for easy reaching. Uncover dough, dip your hand in water and stretch one side of dough up and over to meet opposite side; turn bowl 90°. Repeat 3 more times, turning bowl 90° after each fold. (This constitutes 1 full fold.) If dough doesn’t always stretch to meet opposite side, just aim for the middle. Wet your hands and shake off excess water any time dough begins to feel sticky. Cover dough and let sit 30 minutes (set a timer). Repeat folding process to make 1 full fold. Re-cover and let dough sit another 30 minutes. Repeat folding process and resting one more time. By the last fold, dough should be significantly smoother and tighter.

It has been revealed that transfer dough to a generously floured surface, dust with flour, and shape into a tight ball. Dust dough with more flour. Dust a kitchen towel with flour and place inside a high-sided bowl to line. Arrange dough, seam side up, in bowl on top of towel. Tightly cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit in a warm spot until puffy, about 45 minutes.

Industry observers note that place a rack in middle of oven, then set a large ovenproof Dutch oven with a lid on it; preheat oven to 400°. Place a 12" square of parchment paper on a flat surface. Cut a 2"-long slit in each corner toward the center. Very carefully, tip dough out onto center of parchment, trying your best not to deflate it or ruin its shape. (It’s easiest to place parchment on a flat plate so you can easily turn dough out of bowl.) Working very promptly and using a pair of kitchen shears lightly coated in vegetable oil, cut an X in center of bread. Remove pot from oven and very carefully lower dough into pot. Cover pot and return to oven.

Sources indicate that bake bread 35 minutes. Uncover pot, reduce oven temperature to 375°, and continue to bake bread until crust is deeply browned, 35–40 minutes more. Carefully tip loaf out onto a wire rack and let cool at least 1 hour before slicing.

Do Ahead: Bread can be baked 3 days ahead. Let cool completely; store airtight at room temperature.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that christmas might get the lights, presents, and monthlong buildup, but Ina Garten has a few thoughts about which holiday really deserves the fuss. And if a certain Thanksgiving side dish comes up in conversation, the Barefoot Contessa’s face might tell you everything you need to know.

In a recent development, during the November 18 episode of her Happy Hour with Ina Garten podcast, the cookbook author asked guest Rose Byrne about her first Thanksgiving in the United States. The Australian actress recalled attending a Friendsgiving, with everyone contributing something to the meal, and Garten immediately wanted to know whether the whole thing had been organized in advance or “if everyone just showed up with string beans.”.

Things got even funnier when Byrne mentioned candied yams topped with marshmallows, something she found “pretty weird.” Garten visibly grimaced at the mention of the dish, chuckling before describing them as “very American." Judging by that expression alone, I wouldn't expect to find the dish making an appearance at her next dinner party.

Garten's feelings about Thanksgiving itself, however, are considerably warmer, especially when compared to Christmas.

Recent findings suggest that "Thanksgiving is just quiet. It's all that one day and it's all about the food," she explained, pointing out that Christmas comes with gifts, parties, and a whole lot more going on.

It makes sense coming from someone who’s built an entire career around bringing people together over a good meal. And we already know Garten’s enthusiasm for Thanksgiving extends beyond what’s on the plate. Last year, she shared her favorite wines to serve with Thanksgiving dinner, including Morgon, a lighter French red from the Beaujolais region, and white Burgundies like Meursault or Montrachet to accompany the turkey. She also likes a Sonoma Valley Pinot Noir, giving the American holiday a little hometown representation in the wine department.

At least now I know that if I ever get invited to Thanksgiving at Ina’s, I'll gladly let her handle the wine—and I know to keep the marshmallow-topped yams at home.

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (623 w)

Latest Update: The 7 Most Common Mistakes Home Cooks Make When Cooking Mashed Potatoes

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (623 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Delish

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that in a traditional Thanksgiving meal, mashed potatoes are a seemingly simple side dish that does a lot of heavy lifting.
  • According to recent reports, mashed potatoes prove you can transform even the humblest ingredients into something magical.
  • Thankfully, those mistakes are 100% avoidable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that in a traditional Thanksgiving meal, mashed potatoes are a seemingly simple side dish that does a lot of heavy lifting. They're the perfect vessel for a puddle of gravy, and they’re a creamy complement to everything else on your plate—yes, even your aunt's questionable green bean casserole.

According to recent reports, mashed potatoes prove you can transform even the humblest ingredients into something magical. And yet, we've all somehow still eaten bad ones. With a recipe this basic, even the smallest mistakes have nowhere to hide.

Thankfully, those mistakes are 100% avoidable. We rounded up the most common ways to mess up mashed potatoes so that yours turn out as delicious as possible this holiday season.

It has been revealed that it doesn’t matter if you cut your potatoes into a fine dice or rough chunks. Whatever size you pick, stick with it. Making sure your potato pieces are roughly the same size will help them all cook at the same rate. If your knife work is haphazard, you may end up with some pieces that are perfectly cooked, others that are waterlogged and mushy, and some that are still firm in the center.

In a recent development, like pasta, potatoes need a good amount of seasoning to really shine—which is why salting the cooking water is so crucial. You can be generous with the salt, since much of it stays in the water and ends up going down the drain. When you start seasoning early in the cooking process, it’s easier to build flavor and adjust as you go.

In the hustle of cooking all of your Thanksgiving dishes, you may be tempted to boil your potatoes ahead of time and mash them later in the day. But it’s always better to work with potatoes while they’re still hot and easier to mash. Waiting until they’re cool will likely require far more elbow grease—and you’ll still end up with uneven chunks.

Recent findings suggest that A smooth, creamy mash is the height of decadence. To make sure the potatoes are lump-free, some people may reach for a blender—but this is one of the most consequential mistakes you can make. Potatoes are naturally starchy, and the more you work them, the more starch gets released from their cell walls. Breaking out the blender may be well-intentioned, but it can leave you with potatoes that are gummy and gluey. Instead, opt for the right tool, like a hand masher, food mill, or potato ricer.

Industry observers note that another important thing to consider is that potato starches continue absorbing moisture as mashed potatoes sit. They can soak up the milk you’ve added, leaving your potatoes dry and dense. Don’t be afraid to add more liquid—or at least keep some extra on hand to loosen up your mash before serving.

Recent findings suggest that anthony Bourdain famously pointed to generous amounts of salt and butter as part of what makes restaurant food taste so good. That’s especially true for mashed potatoes. You may be scared to add more than a light sprinkle of salt, but don’t forget to taste and adjust the seasoning before serving. A little extra salt can make all the difference for your Thanksgiving dinner.

Whether you’re feeding your immediate family or a small army, you should always make a massive batch of mashed potatoes. This side is one of the most popular components of a Thanksgiving menu, so it never hurts to make extra. It’s also one of the most versatile dishes for repurposing leftovers. You can transform them into gnocchi, shepherd’s pie, or crispy fried croquettes. It may require more mashing in the moment, but your future self will thank you.

Cyber Monday lands on November 30 this year, the Monday after Thanksgiving. Most brands keep the deals rolling through the week—but that doesn't mean a deal will last all day, so act fast.

Are deals better on Black Friday or Cyber Monday?

Strategy for large retailers and more-established brands to offer deals on Black Friday, and smaller menswear boutiques to hold out for Cyber Monday. Weddings during the holiday season come with a built-in sense of joy. The venue is likely already decked out in garlands and candlelight, everyone is in a celebratory mood, and if the date falls on Fresh Year’s Eve, there’s a midnight countdown baked right into the reception. Your outfit should match that energy. While standard winter guest attire often leans moody, a December through February fête (don’t forget about Valentine’s Day nuptials!) leaves plenty of room to play—think rich textures, high-shine finishes, and statement silhouettes.

As a bridal stylist, I always recommend letting the calendar dictate your palette. A Christmastime wedding begs for jewel tones and seasonal classics like cranberry red, deep emerald, and antique gold—all of which you’ll find at labels like Christopher John Rogers, Posse, and Simkhai. A Latest Year’s Eve ceremony, on the other hand, calls for anything that catches the light and has movement for the dance floor, from Altuzarra’s gold gown done up in cascading paillettes to Kallmeyer’s swingy fringe. Even a strict black-tie dress code can get a festive upgrade: Trade a standard black gown for a golden lamé maxi courtesy of Ulla Johnson. (Just be sure to check the couple’s wedding website for any specific color requests.).

Of course, a few standard wedding-guest rules still hold true. Steer clear of anything that reads as bridal—that includes winter white, no matter how tempting a cream silk slip might be. Skip the costume-like details, too: A ruby-red J.Crew mini feels spirited, while a tinsel-trimmed ensemble in the same shade can rapidly veer kitschy. Beyond that, pay attention to the dress code, as that will dictate your hemline; minis and midis are fair game for less formal invitations, especially when paired with tights and a great heel. And don’t forget about a chic evening coat that’ll tie your outfit together.

Now that you know the basics, it’s time for the fun part. Browse our edit of the 30 best dresses for every holiday wedding on your calendar this winter.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s getting increasingly difficult to keep up with all the limited-edition tumblers, advent calendars, and seasonal releases that disappear off shelves before you’ve finished your morning coffee. And now IHOP is giving breakfast lovers another reason to make room in their kitchen cabinets.

It has been revealed that delish can exclusively reveal that IHOP is launching its first-ever Collector's Holiday Mug on Monday, November 30, with the mugs being sold at participating restaurants nationwide. It’s also the very first time the pancake chain has ventured into selling merchandise directly to customers—and, as it turns out, the idea has been brewing for quite some time.

According to Samantha Strong, IHOP’s executive director of brand calendar strategy, the firm has heard from enough coffee-loving customers over the years to realize there was an actual appetite for owning an IHOP mug. “What started as a frequent question has grown into a genuine fan obsession,” she said, and this holiday release is now the company's first attempt to turn that enthusiasm into something people can actually buy.

In a recent development, IHOP claims coffee is its second best-selling menu item, which means an awful lot of people have spent their mornings clutching one of those mugs while waiting for breakfast. But before you start planning an entire IHOP-themed kitchen makeover, know that each participating location will have just 24 (yes, only 24!) mugs available. Once they're gone, they’re gone, at least as far as this limited-time release is concerned.

There's certainly no shortage of things to collect this holiday season, but at least this one’s something you can actually put to use while doing some damage to a stack of pancakes.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bernie Moreno will chair the National Republican Senatorial Committee during the 2028 cycle.
  • In a recent development, house and Senate Republicans picked their fresh campaign chiefs Tuesday, tasking Ohio Sen.
  • In their new positions, both will spearhead Republicans’ push to win back majorities on Capitol Hill after Democrats seized control of both chambers of Congress by flipping more than 40 House seats and at least seven Senate seats in last week’s midterm elections.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ohio Sen. Bernie Moreno will chair the National Republican Senatorial Committee during the 2028 cycle. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call file photo).

In a recent development, house and Senate Republicans picked their fresh campaign chiefs Tuesday, tasking Ohio Sen. Bernie Moreno and Georgia Rep. Brian Jack with leading the GOP campaign arms for the 2028 election cycle.

In their new positions, both will spearhead Republicans’ push to win back majorities on Capitol Hill after Democrats seized control of both chambers of Congress by flipping more than 40 House seats and at least seven Senate seats in last week’s midterm elections.

Republicans returned to Capitol Hill this week still reeling from their losses but resisted calls to delay Tuesday’s leadership elections. In the Senate, South Dakota’s John Thune was reelected Republican leader without any opposition, while Ohio Rep. Jim Jordan defeated Louisiana Rep. Steve Scalise in a closed-door, secret-ballot election to lead House Republicans next year.

According to recent reports, moreno will succeed South Carolina Sen. Tim Scott as chair of the National Republican Senatorial Committee.

“Republicans must enter this next election clear-eyed: the road ahead back to a Republican Senate majority will by no means be easy but the fight has never been so notable,” the Ohio senator noted in a statement.

Speaking to reporters on Capitol Hill, Moreno described his new role as “a hell of a job.” He noted Republicans would be “absolute savages” on ending government corruption and continuing “to work for the American people.”.

“I suspect the best tailwind we’ll have is that the Democrats will learn all the wrong lessons,” he told reporters.

Sources indicate that moreno, a close ally of President Donald Trump, is currently serving his first term. He first ran for Senate during the 2022 cycle but dropped out of a crowded GOP primary eventually won by JD Vance. Two years later, buoyed by an endorsement from Trump, he won a contested primary for the state’s other Senate seat and went on to oust Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown that fall.

Industry observers note that brown is poised to return to the Senate after defeating appointed Republican Sen. Jon Husted last week in a special election for the remaining Senate term of Vice President Vance. While Ohio has swung heavily toward Republicans over the past decade, Democrats scored substantial wins in the Buckeye State last week, winning several statewide offices and flipping three seats in the U.S. House.

But assuming he runs again for a full term, Brown will be on the ballot in 2028, setting up what’s likely to be a tense home-state fight.

In an apparent reference to the returning Brown, Moreno offered some Washington advice Tuesday: “Make sure you rent. Do not buy.”.

The 2028 Senate map gives Republican pickup opportunities in a handful of swing states, including Arizona, Georgia, Nevada, Newly introduced Hampshire and Pennsylvania. The party will also be defending battleground seats in Alaska, Iowa, North Carolina and Wisconsin. Also on the Senate ballot are races for Republican-held seats in Kansas and South Carolina, where Democrats scored surprise wins last week.

Recent findings suggest that on the House side, Jack defeated Indiana Rep. Rudy Yakym III to become the next chairman of the National Republican Congressional Committee. He takes office after one of the worst elections for the GOP in recent decades and will succeed outgoing NRCC Chair Richard Hudson, who lost his own North Carolina seat last week.

Industry observers note that house Republicans face the tough task of cutting into Democrats’ 40-plus-seat majority next cycle. But the party will have a slew of pickup opportunities, given the sheer number of seats Democrats won in historically red territory this year.

In a recent development, like Moreno, Jack was first elected to Congress 2024, leveraging a close relationship with Trump to win an open seat outside Atlanta. He previously was White House director of political affairs during Trump’s first term and was a senior adviser to the president’s 2024 campaign. Over the past two years, he served as the NRCC’s recruitment chair.

Savannah Behrmann contributed to this report.

Black Friday is the Friday after Thanksgiving, which means that it falls on November 27 this year. But Black Friday deals are no longer confined to the single day, or even the weekend. Discounts start prior to Thanksgiving, and nearly every one lasts until at least that following Monday. Mr. Porter’s Black Friday sale kicked off on Monday, and should run through the weekend at the very least.

In a recent development, cyber Monday traditionally happens the Monday after Black Friday, which means that it’s on November 30 this year. If prior years are any indication, Mr. Porter will surely be continuing their sale through Cyber Monday. But if you’re looking to take full advantage of deals, we wouldn’t advise waiting all the way until then—Mr. Porter is a big store, but they don’t always have a ton of each product available.

What are the best brands to shop at Mr Porter?

We truly do like most of the brands that you’ll see gracing the digital racks at Mr. Porter, but we’d be lying if we mentioned we didn’t have our favorites. That list includes usual suspects—like Dries Van Noten, The Row, Bode, Trickers, Kapital, Mackintosh, Drake’s, Our Legacy, Wales Bonner—but also some lesser-known imprints, like Beams Plus, Barena Venezia, Stòffa, Ghaia Cashmere, OrSlow and De Bonne Facture. And then we also have our favorite crunchy and/or small-batch labels, like Kartik Research, Story MFG and The Elder Statesman, to name a few. (We missed some, but that’s a good problem not a bad one.).

Will Mr Porter have a Cyber Monday sale?

Recent findings suggest that the short answer is yes, they will. The longer answer is that it will most likely roll over from Black Friday, with some promotions specifically tailored for Cyber Monday. It could absolutely increase, or adjust a bit, so make sure you check back, but—once again—nothing on sale is guaranteed to last, so it’s best to move on the things you’re into.

#170492. Welcome to Wonder by Josh Aronson

Welcome to Wonder by Josh Aronson

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1470 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that vizcaya is a fantasy, even by Miami standards.
  • According to recent reports, I grew up in South Florida.
  • Photographs have helped shape the way we see Vizcaya from its earliest days.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Words and images by Josh Aronson.

It has been revealed that vizcaya is a fantasy, even by Miami standards. I found myself wondering who belongs to it. Here was a forest in the middle of Miami, and beyond it, a house that seemed to have arrived from another time and place. I've always found that meeting a little magical. But I've come to understand how quickly the Florida landscape can change. The longer I spent at Vizcaya, the more I wondered how a photograph might hold some of that feeling, and what it might ask us to protect.

According to recent reports, I grew up in South Florida. My family moved here from Toronto when I was three, and we didn't have roots here before us. I've often felt both at home in Miami and curious about my place within it. Vizcaya was part of the city's imagination long before I was invited to make pictures here. To contribute to its story as an artist felt almost difficult to believe.

Photographs have helped shape the way we see Vizcaya from its earliest days. In 1917, Mattie Edwards Hewitt photographed the estate for an matter of Architectural Review devoted to the house and gardens. Her images offered a vision of the world James Deering, Vizcaya's founder, and his collaborators had brought into being on the shore of Biscayne Bay. Today, people come here with cameras for quinceañeras, engagements, weddings, and family portraits. Those pictures find their way into albums and onto walls, carrying a little piece of Vizcaya into homes across Miami.

Industry observers note that for Welcome to Wonder, I made a fresh body of photographs featuring people, animals, and landscapes across Florida. At Vizcaya, the images appear in circular frames around trees and on large banners suspended overhead, along paths that are free to walk seven days a week.

Recent findings suggest that while preparing for Welcome to Wonder, I spent time looking through the estate's archive. In many of the images, people of color appeared working on or caring for the property. I began thinking about what other photographs could exist alongside them: images of young people from Miami's many communities at rest, in play, at ease in the landscape. Who gets to be seen enjoying a place like this? Who gets to imagine that it belongs to them, too?

These questions have been with me throughout my practice, from Tropicana to Florida Boys. I've traveled the state with groups of young men, making photographs in springs, swamps, forests, and along backroads. Many of us grew up in Miami and were encountering these places together for the first time. I would arrive with an idea for a scene, but the pictures were shaped by the people who came along and what the landscape offered us. I've returned to places I'd scouted and found a body of water had dried up or a shoreline had shifted. Those changes stay with me. The places that feel so expansive and enduring can be fragile, too.

Recent findings suggest that I think often about Naomi Fisher's Cibachromes and Hernan Bas' paintings, the tension and theatricality their subjects seemed to find together in the landscape. Those photographs and paintings helped me imagine what it might mean to create a fresh world with other people, and make an image of it. With Florida Boys, I wanted to picture young men who could be tender with one another, who could rest, who could be curious. Making the photographs gave us a reason to go out and experience something together. What began as an imagined scene became part of our lives.

It has been revealed that at Vizcaya, that world began to grow. I found myself wondering what might have happened if, after Deering died, a band of young people had moved into the estate. Who would they have loved? What would their days have looked like? What would they have discovered in the trees and along the water? I began to see the photographs as a kind of fictional archive, evidence of encounters that might have taken place here. Some pictures were made at Vizcaya; others were made elsewhere in South Florida. Together, they allowed me to imagine a landscape without the boundaries of a single property or moment in time.

According to recent reports, for this project, I also photographed young mothers, young fathers, and young families. I thought about the lives a photograph can have after it is made. A child might one day look at an image and see their parent as a young person. A mother might see something of her own family in the gesture of someone she has never met. The photograph becomes a kind of mirror, reflecting something different depending on who we are and where we stand in our lives. I hope these pictures hold a little of that possibility for the people in them, the way they do for me.

I thought, too, about Deering. He never married, and questions about his sexuality have followed him long after his death. The historical record doesn't give us a conclusive answer. As an artist, I'm interested in the space between what a life contains and what the archive preserves. We do know that Paul Chalfin, Vizcaya's artistic director, lived here with his partner, Louis Koons. I wonder about the other private worlds that might have existed here, leaving traces we may never find.

Sources indicate that on the Hammock Paths, photographs printed on acrylic are held in circular frames that appear to float around the trees. Along the Metrorail route, larger images hang in the canopy, printed on mesh that lets the light filter through. I was thinking about the symmetry of Vizcaya's gardens, but also about the way a circle has no beginning and no end. You can walk around a ring and find a photograph on either side. You can enter the path from the city or come upon it as you leave the museum. The images can be discovered, passed by, returned to, seen differently on any day.

Industry observers note that both the Hammock Paths and the Metrorail site are free and open to the public seven days a week. You don't need a ticket to spend time with the work. In a city where so much can feel out of reach, that matters. I think about the people who walk these paths every day, on their way home or with a dog, and the people who might encounter the photographs without knowing anything about Florida Boys or my collaborators. The possibility that an image could become part of someone's daily life feels like a gift and a responsibility.

Across the city, at MOCA, my commission A Sudden Leap rises from the plaza's reflecting pool. Four photographs of Florida's natural world have become sails, suspended above the water. Some of these quieter images grew out of the same journeys that gave me Florida Boys. There are no people in the pictures, but there are people moving around them, bringing their own histories and experiences to the work. I think about the sails and the journeys that have brought so many of us to Miami, including my own family. I hope the photographs might make someone want to see these places and care about what happens to them.

To have work at Vizcaya and at MOCA, my neighborhood museum, at the same time is something I'm still trying to take in. Both have given me a way to look at the place that raised me, and to offer those images back to the people who live here. The photographs at Vizcaya will eventually come down, and people will continue to walk these paths. I hope someone remembers an image the next time they pass a tree, or carries a little of the feeling of this place back into the city with them. What we choose to see, I've come to believe, has something to do with what we choose to hold dear.

According to recent reports, josh Aronson's Welcome to Wonder is on view at Vizcaya Museum and Gardens, Miami through May 24, 2027. A Sudden Leap, Aronson's MOCA Art on the Plaza public artwork commission, is on view at the Museum of Contemporary Art, North Miami through January 17, 2027.

Sources indicate that josh Aronson (b. 1994, Canada) is a Miami-based artist whose work explores masculinity and landscape in the American South. His photographs have appeared in The New York Times, The New Yorker, The Paris Review, Frieze, and Apartamento, among others. His first solo museum exhibition, Welcome to Wonder, is on view at Vizcaya Museum and Gardens, Miami, and his first museum-commissioned public artwork, A Sudden Leap, is on view at the Museum of Contemporary Art, North Miami. www.josharonson.us.

ELLE Escapes: London

📅 20 Apr 2022 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1587 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A trip to London may conjure two different and somewhat competing vacation fantasies: the first, a more royal-inspired vision, with fancy tea parties, shopping at Selfridges, and photos outside Kensington Palace, and the second somewhat grungier, filled with smoky Camden bars and vinyl shopping in Soho.
  • It has been revealed that there’s no better way to see London than riding along the Thames itself.
  • Industry observers note that in 2000, Swedish supergroup ABBA famously turned down a $1 billion offer to reunite.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A trip to London may conjure two different and somewhat competing vacation fantasies: the first, a more royal-inspired vision, with fancy tea parties, shopping at Selfridges, and photos outside Kensington Palace, and the second somewhat grungier, filled with smoky Camden bars and vinyl shopping in Soho. Why not do both? For ELLE Escapes, we compiled some of our favorite spots for making the most of your journey across the pond. London’s calling—here’s where to eat, drink, stay, and shop when you answer.

It has been revealed that there’s no better way to see London than riding along the Thames itself. The Tower of London offers its own 40-minute river cruise on the country’s first electric passenger boat. Sit back, relax, and listen as the boat’s lively guide breaks down the backstory of the city’s famed bridges and buildings—and takes any questions you have about the city’s history. Bad weather isn’t an concern aboard this ship, thanks to its see-through canopy roof and indoor section. Want to see London at its absolute best? Try booking after sunset during the cooler months so you can take in the city’s lights.

Industry observers note that in 2000, Swedish supergroup ABBA famously turned down a $1 billion offer to reunite. Now, thanks to cutting-edge technology, you can see them together again—sort of. ABBA Voyage is a first-of-its-kind live show featuring digital versions of Agnetha Fältskog, Björn Ulvaeus, Benny Andersson, and Anni-Frid Lyngstad, performing alongside a live 10-piece band at their custom-built ABBA Arena in Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park, London. It’s truly an experience like no other.

A trip here never feels complete without a bit of vintage shopping. Picture this: you’re wandering through Hackney when a pair of vintage Issey Miyake cropped cargos catches your eye in the window. Step inside and you’ll discover Files London, a concept archive store in East London that feels like a true treasure trove. Specializing in Japanese, French, British, Belgian, and Italian designers, the shop offers a meticulously curated selection that fashion lovers will swoon over. The space itself is just as striking as the clothes, making the visit an experience in its own right. And while this city is brimming with vintage and thrift gems, a stop at Files pairs perfectly with an afternoon of shopping in nearby Shoreditch or Soho. Pro tip: bring an extra bag—or at least leave some room in your suitcase—for all the newly introduced finds.

It’s not a visit to London without afternoon tea, and Pan Pacific London’s offering truly raises the bar. The meal starts with the server unfolding and placing your napkin on your lap, a British tradition. Then comes the amuse-bouche course with its standout pork and apricot sausage roll. The sandwich course follows—four different types, with the menu changing seasonally—along with a palate cleanser (a cold jasmine infusion in the summer) before the sweets take center stage. First, you’ll munch on scones with clotted cream, citrus curd, and jam. But save room for the grand finale: a gorgeous array of four small pastries. For those in town for the holidays, the Christmas tea includes a mini yule log and a coconut snowman macaron that’s almost too adorable to eat. Almost.

It has been revealed that your culinary experience isn’t complete without a Sunday roast. For that and a whole lot more, try The Grill at The Dorchester, a landmark restaurant that first opened its doors in 1931. Expect modern takes on classic fare—including but not limited to a carving trolley. (We’re salivating too.).

Located on the 60th floor of one of London’s tallest buildings in Mayfair, Gordon Ramsay’s fresh Asian-inspired restaurant Lucky Cat offers a feast for the eyes as much as for the stomach. Dine alongside panoramic views of the city, which really stand out at night. For those hungry but unsure where to begin with the restaurant’s extensive options, Lucky Cat offers three different tasting menus. Notable dishes include its yellowtail tartare topped with caviar and yuzu, along with its melt-in-your-mouth grilled miso salmon and tender scallops with yuzu and sweet corn. Don’t skip dessert; the mango cheesecake, designed to be a trompe l’œil of the fruit with its white chocolate shell, is a light but special way to cap off a decadent meal.

By Malene Birger Blanca Fringed Boucle Cardigan.

By Malene Birger Belicia Fringed Mini Skirt.

It has been revealed that mr. Lyan (bartender Ryan Chetiyawardana’s nom célèbre) knows how to make a good cocktail, be it at Washington, D.C.’s Silver Lyan or London’s Lyaness. The U.K. outpost, tucked into South Bank’s Sea Containers building, has some of the most innovative drinks you’ll find in the city, all with cheeky backstories written on the menu for you to discover. While the bar’s offerings do change, the Rainwater Fix was one of its best from its Collaboration 2.0 menu. The tropical mixture, featuring Patrón blanco tequila (or Tropic All in its mocktail version), pineapple shio, Capreolus eau de vie, and passion fruit wine, will transport you back to summer with one sip—no matter what the weather is outside. There’s also plenty of food to enjoy, like sea bass ceviche tacos, fries, and English coastal oysters served with a black currant mignonette.

Fitz’s, named after the hotel’s original architect, is a cocktail bar that turns drinking into a playful experience. Inside, a striking, contemporary interior nods to the hotel’s historic roots, while a unique UV-light menu adds a theatrical twist. With inventive cocktails and attentive service, Fitz’s is an ideal spot for a pre-dinner drink or a stylish night out in Bloomsbury.

Industry observers note that it’s not a wild night out in London if you don’t, at some point, find yourself in Shoreditch—and Tonight Josephine is the perfect stop for maximalists in search of an Instagrammable end to the evening. The décor channels early-aughts club life, complete with lots of hot pink, neon signs, and—naturally—a photo booth.

Amina Muaddi Jamie Leather Mules.

Industry observers note that hyde Park is easily one of the most beautiful places in central London—so why not stay at an iconic hotel with panoramic views of it? The Royal Lancaster London, a member of Preferred Hotels & Resorts, spans 18 floors and features 411 rooms that blend timeless elegance with modern comfort. Following a $115 million renovation, the hotel now boasts sleek, light-filled interiors, marble bathrooms, rainfall showers, and a warm, welcoming atmosphere. Book a deluxe room or suite for wraparound windows offering a vantage point that stretches from Wembley Stadium to the Shard. Perfectly positioned on the edge of Hyde Park, the hotel puts you within walking distance of some of London’s top destinations—Knightsbridge and Harrods across the park, or Oxford Street and Marble Arch just 15 minutes away on foot.

Kimpton Fitzroy blends historic grandeur with playful modernity. From its terracotta-adorned façade to the moody marble archways and astrological-tiled floors, the hotel evokes a mythical, storied past. Step inside the rooms, and the atmosphere transforms—each suite is uniquely styled, combining contemporary design with whimsical details. It’s the kind of place that feels like a home away from home. The location is a dream for avid explorers: perched on Russell Square in the heart of Bloomsbury, the hotel offers easy access to the British Museum, Oxford Street, boutique shops in Soho, and more. Harry Potter fans are just minutes from Platform 9¾, while a short bus ride north will take you to Primrose Hill, where the iconic scene from One Day was filmed.

Nestled in the stunning former Whiteleys department store building, Six Senses London is far more than just a beautiful place to wake up in Bayswater. The hotel is dedicated to your wellness—be it in the small details like its pillow menu and “ginger hello” check-in treats (including its locally sourced ginger kombucha and chocolate orange truffles) or bigger ones like its innovative spa, where the team will craft a blueprint to help your body best recover based on your key biomarker readings, using the facility’s 13 treatment rooms. While there’s plenty to explore in the picturesque Kensington Gardens and Notting Hill nearby, there’s a good reason to stay in, too. Standout experiences include booking an appointment at the alchemy bar, where a skilled herbalist will make you a tea or tonic to address any health concerns, and having a leisurely dinner at the hotel’s Whiteley’s Kitchen. The produce-driven restaurant has an incredible “Trust the Chef” tasting menu where thoughtful dishes like mushroom tagliatelle with coffee butter and butterflied sea bass with sea fennel will enchant you with every bite.

AKT London The Haze: A Deodorizing Body Mist.

If you own an AKT deodorant, you know the brand doesn’t skimp on delectable scents. Its deodorizing mists are no different, using the same deodorant formula to keep you fresh and smelling good from head to toe.

Violette Fr Lip Nectar Hydrating Lip Stain.

In a recent development, skip the constant touch-ups and opt for a formula that looks good at the start, middle, and end of your day. Lips look visibly plump and juicy, thanks to a hyaluronic acid and squalane base.

Yves Saint Laurent Libre Santal Couture Eau de Parfum.

According to recent reports, at the base of Libre Santal is sandalwood, which transforms this perfume into a deep, sensual woody aroma. It has its bright moments at first, with a soft lavender and orange blossom opening. As it settles, it feels warmer and cozier, perfect for London’s chilly days and nights.

Additional reporting by Claire Stern Milch and Leah Romero.

People Are Calling The Day Before Thanksgiving ‘Green Wednesday’—And It’s Becoming A Huge Holiday
